query: Query: dopamine antagonists [SEP] Dopamine antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate dopamine receptors, thereby blocking the actions of dopamine or exogenous agonists. Many drugs used in the treatment of psychotic disorders (antipsychotic agents) are dopamine antagonists, although their therapeutic effects may be due to long-term adjustments of the brain rather than to the acute effects of blocking dopamine receptors. Dopamine antagonists have been used for several other clinical purposes including as antiemetics, in the treatment of Tourette syndrome, and for hiccup. Dopamine receptor blockade is associated with neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

name: dose fractionation , radiation
query: Query: dose fractionation , radiation [SEP] Radiation dose fractionation is administration of the total dose of radiation (radiation dosage) in parts, at timed intervals.

name: drugs , essential
query: Query: drugs , essential [SEP] Essential drugs is drugs considered essential to meet the health needs of a population as well as to control drug costs.

name: drug trafficking
query: Query: drug trafficking [SEP] Drug trafficking is the illegal acquisition, sale, production, transport, movement, and distribution of controlled substances such as narcotics.

name: dual use research
query: Query: dual use research [SEP] Dual use research is concept relating to technologies and/or information emanating from research that holds the potential for both benevolent and malevolent applications to humanity and the environment.

name: ear , inner
query: Query: ear , inner [SEP] Inner ear is the essential part of the hearing organ consists of two labyrinthine compartments: the bony labyrinthine and the membranous labyrinth. The bony labyrinth is a complex of three interconnecting cavities or spaces (cochlea; vestibular labyrinth; and semicircular canals) in the temporal bone. Within the bony labyrinth lies the membranous labyrinth which is a complex of sacs and tubules (cochlear duct; saccule and utricle; and semicircular ducts) forming a continuous space enclosed by epithelium and connective tissue. These spaces are filled with labyrinthine fluids of various compositions.

name: ear , middle
query: Query: ear , middle [SEP] Middle ear is the space and structures directly internal to the tympanic membrane and external to the inner ear (labyrinth). Its major components include the auditory ossicles and the eustachian tube that connects the cavity of middle ear (tympanic cavity) to the upper part of the throat.

name: early growth response protein 3
query: Query: early growth response protein 3 [SEP] Early growth response protein 3 is an early growth response transcription factor that is essential for the development of muscle spindles.

name: early termination of clinical trials
query: Query: early termination of clinical trials [SEP] Early termination of clinical trials is earlier than planned termination of clinical trials.

name: editorial
query: Query: editorial [SEP] Editorial is work consisting of a statement of the opinions, beliefs, and policy of the editor or publisher of a journal, usually on current matters of medical or scientific significance to the medical community or society at large. The editorials published by editors of journals representing the official organ of a society or organization are generally substantive.

name: egg yolk
query: Query: egg yolk [SEP] Egg yolk is cytoplasm stored in an egg that contains nutritional reserves for the developing embryo. It is rich in polysaccharides, lipids, and proteins.

name: elbow prosthesis
query: Query: elbow prosthesis [SEP] Elbow prosthesis is replacement for an elbow joint.

name: elder abuse
query: Query: elder abuse [SEP] Elder abuse is emotional, nutritional, financial, or physical maltreatment, exploitation, or abandonment of the older person generally by family members or by institutional personnel.

name: electric capacitance
query: Query: electric capacitance [SEP] Electric capacitance is the ability of a substrate to retain an electrical charge.

name: electrodes , implanted
query: Query: electrodes , implanted [SEP] Implanted electrodes is surgically placed electric conductors through which electric stimulation is delivered to or electrical activity is recorded from a specific point inside the body.

name: embryo implantation , delayed
query: Query: embryo implantation , delayed [SEP] Delayed embryo implantation is delay in the attachment and implantation of blastocyst to the uterine endometrium. The blastocyst remains unattached beyond the normal duration thus delaying embryonic development.

name: employee performance appraisal
query: Query: employee performance appraisal [SEP] Employee performance appraisal is the assessment of the functioning of an employee in relation to work.

name: employee retirement income security act
query: Query: employee retirement income security act [SEP] Employee retirement income security act is a 1974 Federal act which preempts states' rights with regard to workers' pension benefits and employee benefits. It does not affect the benefits and rights of employees whose employer is self-insured. (From Slee & Slee, Health Care Reform Terms, 1993)

name: endocrinology
query: Query: endocrinology [SEP] Endocrinology is a subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the metabolism, physiology, and disorders of the endocrine system.

name: endothelium , lymphatic
query: Query: endothelium , lymphatic [SEP] Lymphatic endothelium is unbroken cellular lining (intima) of the lymph vessels (e.g., the high endothelial lymphatic venules). It is more permeable than vascular endothelium, lacking selective absorption and functioning mainly to remove plasma proteins that have filtered through the capillaries into the tissue spaces.

name: end stage liver disease
query: Query: end stage liver disease [SEP] End stage liver disease is final stage of a liver disease when the liver failure is irreversible and liver transplantation is needed.

name: entropy
query: Query: entropy [SEP] Entropy is the measure of that part of the heat or energy of a system which is not available to perform work. Entropy increases in all natural (spontaneous and irreversible) processes. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: environmental medicine
query: Query: environmental medicine [SEP] Environmental medicine is medical specialty concerned with environmental factors that may impinge upon human disease, and development of methods for the detection, prevention, and control of environmentally related disease.

name: equipment and supplies utilization
query: Query: equipment and supplies utilization [SEP] Equipment and supplies utilization is extent of use of equipment or supplies. It includes overuse and underuse.

name: erbb receptors
query: Query: erbb receptors [SEP] Erbb receptors is a family of structurally-related cell-surface receptors that signal through an intrinsic protein-tyrosine kinase. The receptors are activated upon binding of specific ligands which include epidermal growth factors, and neuregulins.

name: estrogen receptor antagonists
query: Query: estrogen receptor antagonists [SEP] Estrogen receptor antagonists is compounds and drugs that bind to and block or inhibit the activation of estrogen receptors.

name: estrogen receptor beta
query: Query: estrogen receptor beta [SEP] Estrogen receptor beta is one of the estrogen receptors that has greater affinity for isoflavones than estrogen receptor alpha does. There is great sequence homology with er alpha in the DNA-binding domain but not in the ligand binding and hinge domains.

name: ethics , institutional
query: Query: ethics , institutional [SEP] Institutional ethics is the moral and ethical obligations or responsibilities of institutions.

name: ethylene oxide
query: Query: ethylene oxide [SEP] Ethylene oxide is a colorless and flammable gas at room temperature and pressure. Ethylene oxide is a bactericidal, fungicidal, and sporicidal disinfectant. It is effective against most micro-organisms, including viruses. It is used as a fumigant for foodstuffs and textiles and as an agent for the gaseous sterilization of heat-labile pharmaceutical and surgical materials. (From Reynolds, Martindale The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p794)

name: evoked potentials , visual
query: Query: evoked potentials , visual [SEP] Visual evoked potentials is the electric response evoked in the cerebral cortex by visual stimulation or stimulation of the visual pathways.

name: excitatory amino acid antagonists
query: Query: excitatory amino acid antagonists [SEP] Excitatory amino acid antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate excitatory amino acid receptors, thereby blocking the actions of agonists.

name: excitatory amino acid transporter 3
query: Query: excitatory amino acid transporter 3 [SEP] Excitatory amino acid transporter 3 is a neuronal and epithelial type glutamate plasma membrane transporter protein.

name: facial muscles
query: Query: facial muscles [SEP] Facial muscles is muscles of facial expression or mimetic muscles that include the numerous muscles supplied by the facial nerve that are attached to and move the skin of the face. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

name: facial paralysis
query: Query: facial paralysis [SEP] Facial paralysis is severe or complete loss of facial muscle motor function. This condition may result from central or peripheral lesions. Damage to cns motor pathways from the cerebral cortex to the facial nuclei in the pons leads to facial weakness that generally spares the forehead muscles. facial nerve diseases generally results in generalized hemifacial weakness. neuromuscular junction diseases and muscular diseases may also cause facial paralysis or paresis.

name: familial primary pulmonary hypertension
query: Query: familial primary pulmonary hypertension [SEP] Familial primary pulmonary hypertension is familial or idiopathic hypertension in the pulmonary circulation which is not secondary to other disease.

name: family health
query: Query: family health [SEP] Family health is the health status of the family as a unit including the impact of the health of one member of the family on the family as a unit and on individual family members; also, the impact of family organization or disorganization on the health status of its members.

name: farmers
query: Query: farmers [SEP] Farmers is persons who cultivate land or crops, or raise livestock.

name: fatty acids , essential
query: Query: fatty acids , essential [SEP] Essential fatty acids is long chain organic acid molecules that must be obtained from the diet. Examples are linoleic acids and linolenic acids.

name: feedback , psychological
query: Query: feedback , psychological [SEP] Psychological feedback is a mechanism of information stimulus and response that may control subsequent behavior, cognition, perception, or performance. (From apa Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

name: fertile period
query: Query: fertile period [SEP] Fertile period is the period in the menstrual cycle that is optimal for fertilization of the ovum and yielding pregnancy. The duration of fertile period depends on the life span of male gametes within the female reproductive tract and the time of ovulation. It usually begins a few days before ovulation and ends on the day of ovulation.

name: fetal monitoring
query: Query: fetal monitoring [SEP] Fetal monitoring is physiologic or biochemical monitoring of the fetus. It is usually done during labor, obstetric and may be performed in conjunction with the monitoring of uterine activity. It may also be performed prenatally as when the mother is undergoing surgery.

name: fibroblast growth factor 5
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 5 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 5 is a fibroblast growth factor that may play a role in regulation of hair follicle phenotype. Spontaneous mutation of the gene for this protein results in a strain of mice with abnormally long hair, referred to as angora mice.

name: food inspection
query: Query: food inspection [SEP] Food inspection is examination of foods to assure wholesome and clean products free from unsafe microbes or chemical contamination, natural or added deleterious substances, and decomposition during production, processing, packaging, etc.

name: foot
query: Query: foot [SEP] Foot is the distal extremity of the leg in vertebrates, consisting of the tarsus (ankle); metatarsus; phalanges; and the soft tissues surrounding these bones.

name: foot rot
query: Query: foot rot [SEP] Foot rot is a disease of the horny parts and of the adjacent soft structures of the feet of cattle, swine, and sheep. It is usually caused by Corynebacterium pyogenes or Bacteroides nodosus (see dichelobacter nodosus). It is also known as interdigital necrobacillosis. (From Black's Veterinary Dictionary, 18th ed)

name: forced expiratory volume
query: Query: forced expiratory volume [SEP] Forced expiratory volume is measure of the maximum amount of air that can be expelled in a given number of seconds during a forced vital capacity determination . It is usually given as fev followed by a subscript indicating the number of seconds over which the measurement is made, although it is sometimes given as a percentage of forced vital capacity.

name: forensic nursing
query: Query: forensic nursing [SEP] Forensic nursing is the application of nursing knowledge to questions of law. It is a specialty of nursing practice involving victims of crime which includes not only attending to the physical and emotional distress of victims, but also the identifying, collecting, and preserving evidence for law enforcement and the criminal justice system.

name: fourier analysis
query: Query: fourier analysis [SEP] Fourier analysis is analysis based on the mathematical function first formulated by Jean-Baptiste-Joseph Fourier in 1807. The function, known as the Fourier transform, describes the sinusoidal pattern of any fluctuating pattern in the physical world in terms of its amplitude and its phase. It has broad applications in biomedicine, e.g., analysis of the x-ray crystallography data pivotal in identifying the double helical nature of dna and in analysis of other molecules, including viruses, and the modified back-projection algorithm universally used in computerized tomography imaging, etc. (From Segen, The Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

name: fractional precipitation
query: Query: fractional precipitation [SEP] Fractional precipitation is a method which uses specific precipitation reactions to separate or collect substances from a solution.

name: fractures , spontaneous
query: Query: fractures , spontaneous [SEP] Spontaneous fractures is fractures occurring as a result of disease of a bone or from some undiscoverable cause, and not due to trauma. (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: fractures , stress
query: Query: fractures , stress [SEP] Stress fractures is fractures due to the strain caused by repetitive exercise. They are thought to arise from a combination of muscle fatigue and bone failure, and occur in situations where bone remodeling predominates over repair. The most common sites of stress fractures are the metatarsus; fibula; tibia; and femoral neck.

name: frontal bone
query: Query: frontal bone [SEP] Frontal bone is the bone that forms the frontal aspect of the skull. Its flat part forms the forehead, articulating inferiorly with the nasal bone and the cheek bone on each side of the face.

name: frozen foods
query: Query: frozen foods [SEP] Frozen foods is foods that are preserved by lowering their storage temperature below the freezing point.

name: fungal capsules
query: Query: fungal capsules [SEP] Fungal capsules is an extracellular layer outside the cell wall of a fungus composed of polysaccharides. It may serve a protective role amongst others.

name: funnel chest
query: Query: funnel chest [SEP] Funnel chest is a developmental anomaly in which the lower sternum is posteriorly dislocated and concavely deformed, resulting in a funnel-shaped thorax.

name: gata transcription factors
query: Query: gata transcription factors [SEP] Gata transcription factors is a family of transcription factors that contain two zinc finger motifs and bind to the dna sequence (a/t)gata(a/g).

name: gene expression regulation , fungal
query: Query: gene expression regulation , fungal [SEP] Fungal gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action in fungi.

name: general adaptation syndrome
query: Query: general adaptation syndrome [SEP] General adaptation syndrome is the sum of all nonspecific systemic reactions of the body to long-continued exposure to systemic stress.

name: general practice , dental
query: Query: general practice , dental [SEP] Dental general practice is nonspecialized dental practice which is concerned with providing primary and continuing dental care.

name: genes , chloroplast
query: Query: genes , chloroplast [SEP] Chloroplast genes is those nucleic acid sequences that function as units of heredity which are located within the chloroplast dna.

name: genes , switch
query: Query: genes , switch [SEP] Switch genes is genes that cause the epigenotype (i.e., the interrelated developmental pathways through which the adult organism is realized) to switch to an alternate cell lineage-related pathway. Switch complexes control the expression of normal functional development as well as oncogenic transformation.

name: gestational sac
query: Query: gestational sac [SEP] Gestational sac is round-shaped structure usually located in the upper fundus of the uterus in early pregnancy. It comprises embryo; amniotic fluid; and yolk sac. It is visible in prenatal ultrasonography by the fifth week of pregnancy. Its size is often used to determine and monitor gestational age; fetal growth; and pregnancy complications.

name: gestational weight gain
query: Query: gestational weight gain [SEP] Gestational weight gain is increase in body weight of the mother during the course of her pregnancy.

name: gift giving
query: Query: gift giving [SEP] Gift giving is the bestowing of tangible or intangible benefits, voluntarily and usually without expectation of anything in return. However, gift giving may be motivated by feelings of altruism or gratitude, by a sense of obligation, or by the hope of receiving something in return.

name: global health
query: Query: global health [SEP] Global health is a multi- and interdisciplinary field concerned with improving health and achieving equity in health for all people. It transcends national boundaries, promotes cooperation and collaboration within and beyond health science fields, and combines population-based disease prevention with individually-based patient care.

name: glycogen storage disease type iv
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type iv [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type iv is an autosomal recessive metabolic disorder due to a deficiency in expression of glycogen branching enzyme 1 (alpha-1,4-glucan-6-alpha-glucosyltransferase), resulting in an accumulation of abnormal glycogen with long outer branches. Clinical features are muscle hypotonia and cirrhosis. Death from liver disease usually occurs before age 2.

name: glycoprotein hormones , alpha subunit
query: Query: glycoprotein hormones , alpha subunit [SEP] Alpha subunit glycoprotein hormones is the alpha chain of pituitary glycoprotein hormones (thyrotropin; follicle stimulating hormone; luteinizing hormone) and the placental chorionic gonadotropin. Within a species, the alpha subunits of these four hormones are identical; the distinct functional characteristics of these glycoprotein hormones are determined by the unique beta subunits. Both subunits, the non-covalently bound heterodimers, are required for full biologic activity.

name: glycosylation
query: Query: glycosylation [SEP] Glycosylation is the chemical or biochemical addition of carbohydrate or glycosyl groups to other chemicals, especially peptides or proteins. Glycosyl transferases are used in this biochemical reaction.

name: grateful med
query: Query: grateful med [SEP] Grateful med is a microcomputer-based software package providing a user-friendly interface to the medlars system of the National Library of Medicine.

name: gravity sensing
query: Query: gravity sensing [SEP] Gravity sensing is process whereby a cell, bodily structure, or organism (animal or plant) receives or detects a gravity stimulus. Gravity sensing plays an important role in the directional growth and development of an organism (gravitropism).

name: gulf war
query: Query: gulf war [SEP] Gulf war is united Nations' action to intervene in conflict between the nation of Kuwait and occupying Iraqi forces, occurring from 1990 through 1991.

name: gynecology
query: Query: gynecology [SEP] Gynecology is a medical-surgical specialty concerned with the physiology and disorders primarily of the female genital tract, as well as female endocrinology and reproductive physiology.

name: hand hygiene
query: Query: hand hygiene [SEP] Hand hygiene is practices involved in preventing the transmission of diseases by hand.

name: hand strength
query: Query: hand strength [SEP] Hand strength is force exerted when gripping or grasping.

name: hawaii
query: Query: hawaii [SEP] Hawaii is a group of islands in Polynesia, in the north central Pacific Ocean, comprising eight major and 114 minor islands, largely volcanic and coral. Its capital is Honolulu. It was first reached by Polynesians about 500 a.d. It was discovered and named the Sandwich Islands in 1778 by Captain Cook. The islands were united under the rule of King Kamehameha 1795-1819 and requested annexation to the United States in 1893 when a provisional government was set up. Hawaii was established as a territory in 1900 and admitted as a state in 1959. The name is from the Polynesian Owhyhii, place of the gods, with reference to the two volcanoes Mauna Kea and Mauna Loa, regarded as the abode of the gods. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p493 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p2330)

name: healthcare common procedure coding system
query: Query: healthcare common procedure coding system [SEP] Healthcare common procedure coding system is uniform method for health care providers and medical suppliers to report professional services, procedures, and supplies. It consists of alphanumeric codes and modifiers for the use of all public and private health insurers. It is developed by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

name: health educators
query: Query: health educators [SEP] Health educators is professionals who plan, organize and direct health education programs for the individual, groups and the community.

name: health plan implementation
query: Query: health plan implementation [SEP] Health plan implementation is those actions designed to carry out recommendations pertaining to health plans or programs.

name: health planning guidelines
query: Query: health planning guidelines [SEP] Health planning guidelines is recommendations for directing health planning functions and policies. These may be mandated by pl93-641 and issued by the Department of Health and Human Services for use by state and local planning agencies.

name: health systems plans
query: Query: health systems plans [SEP] Health systems plans is statements of goals for the delivery of health services pertaining to the Health Systems Agency service area, established under pl 93-641, and consistent with national guidelines for health planning.

name: healthy volunteers
query: Query: healthy volunteers [SEP] Healthy volunteers is persons with no known significant health problems who are recruited to participate in research to test a new drug, device, or intervention as controls for a patient group. (from http://clinicalcenter.nih.gov/recruit/volunteers.html, accessed 2/14/2013)

name: heart aneurysm
query: Query: heart aneurysm [SEP] Heart aneurysm is a localized bulging or dilatation in the muscle wall of a heart (myocardium), usually in the left ventricle. Blood-filled aneurysms are dangerous because they may burst. Fibrous aneurysms interfere with the heart function through the loss of contractility. True aneurysm is bound by the vessel wall or cardiac wall. False aneurysms are hematoma caused by myocardial rupture.

name: hemodialysis solutions
query: Query: hemodialysis solutions [SEP] Hemodialysis solutions is solutions prepared for hemodialysis. The composition of the pre-dialysis solution may be varied in order to determine the effect of solvated metabolites on anoxia, malnutrition, acid-base balance, etc. Of principal interest are the effect of the choice of buffers (e.g., acetate or carbonate), the addition of cations (Na+, k+, Ca2+), and addition of carbohydrates (glucose).

name: hepatitis b antibodies
query: Query: hepatitis b antibodies [SEP] Hepatitis b antibodies is antibodies to the hepatitis b antigens, including antibodies to the surface (Australia) and core of the Dane particle and those to the "e" antigens.

name: high fidelity simulation training
query: Query: high fidelity simulation training [SEP] High fidelity simulation training is a controlled learning environment that closely represents reality.

name: histamine release
query: Query: histamine release [SEP] Histamine release is the secretion of histamine from mast cell and basophil granules by exocytosis. This can be initiated by a number of factors, all of which involve binding of IgE, cross-linked by antigen, to the mast cell or basophil's Fc receptors. Once released, histamine binds to a number of different target cell receptors and exerts a wide variety of effects.

name: history of nursing
query: Query: history of nursing [SEP] History of nursing is study of past events and development in the field of Nursing.

name: holistic health
query: Query: holistic health [SEP] Holistic health is health as viewed from the perspective that humans function as complete, integrated units rather than as aggregates of separate parts.

name: home health nursing
query: Query: home health nursing [SEP] Home health nursing is a nursing specialty in which skilled nursing care is provided to patients in their homes by registered or licensed practical nurses. Home health nursing differs from home nursing in that home health nurses are licensed professionals, while home nursing involves non-professional caregivers.

name: hospital design and construction
query: Query: hospital design and construction [SEP] Hospital design and construction is the architecture, functional design, and construction of hospitals.

name: hospital medicine
query: Query: hospital medicine [SEP] Hospital medicine is the branch of medicine concerned with the delivery of comprehensive medical care to hospitalized patients. Practitioners include physicians and non-physician providers who engage in clinical care, teaching, research, or leadership in the field of general hospital medicine.(from http://www.hospitalmedicine.org/AM/Template.cfm?Section=Hospitalist_Definition)

name: hospitals , community
query: Query: hospitals , community [SEP] Community hospitals is institutions with permanent facilities and organized medical staff which provide the full range of hospital services primarily to a neighborhood area.

name: hospitals , satellite
query: Query: hospitals , satellite [SEP] Satellite hospitals is those hospitals which are extensions of a main hospital and are wholly or partly administered by that hospital.

name: hospital shared services
query: Query: hospital shared services [SEP] Hospital shared services is cooperation among hospitals for the purpose of sharing various departmental services, e.g., pharmacy, laundry, data processing, etc.

name: human body
query: Query: human body [SEP] Human body is the human being as a non-anatomical and non-zoological entity. The emphasis is on the philosophical or artistic treatment of the human being, and includes lay and social attitudes toward the body in history. (From j. Cassedy, nlm History of Medicine Division)

name: hypertensive retinopathy
query: Query: hypertensive retinopathy [SEP] Hypertensive retinopathy is degenerative changes to the retina due to hypertension.

name: iliac vein
query: Query: iliac vein [SEP] Iliac vein is a vein on either side of the body which is formed by the union of the external and internal iliac veins and passes upward to join with its fellow of the opposite side to form the inferior vena cava.

name: immune reconstitution
query: Query: immune reconstitution [SEP] Immune reconstitution is regeneration of normal immune function after immune depleting procedures or infections (e.g., hematopoietic stem cell transplantation). Delayed and incomplete reconstitution of the adaptive immune system in particular involving t-cells is associated with increase or relapse of infection.

name: immunogenicity , vaccine
query: Query: immunogenicity , vaccine [SEP] Vaccine immunogenicity is the capacity of vaccines to stimulate the adaptive immune response to produce antibodies and antigen-specific t-cell responses.

name: immunoglobulin fc fragments
query: Query: immunoglobulin fc fragments [SEP] Immunoglobulin fc fragments is crystallizable fragments composed of the carboxy-terminal halves of both immunoglobulin heavy chains linked to each other by disulfide bonds. Fc fragments contain the carboxy-terminal parts of the heavy chain constant regions that are responsible for the effector functions of an immunoglobulin (complement fixation, binding to the cell membrane via fc receptors, and placental transport). This fragment can be obtained by digestion of immunoglobulins with the proteolytic enzyme papain.

name: immunoglobulin heavy chains
query: Query: immunoglobulin heavy chains [SEP] Immunoglobulin heavy chains is the largest of polypeptide chains comprising immunoglobulins. They contain 450 to 600 amino acid residues per chain, and have molecular weights of 51-72 kDa.

name: implementation science
query: Query: implementation science [SEP] Implementation science is the study of methods to promote the adoption and integration of evidence-based practices, interventions and policies into routine health care and public health settings.

name: industrial oils
query: Query: industrial oils [SEP] Industrial oils is oils which are used in industrial or commercial applications.

name: infection control , dental
query: Query: infection control , dental [SEP] Dental infection control is efforts to prevent and control the spread of infections within dental health facilities or those involving provision of dental care.

name: inflammatory breast neoplasms
query: Query: inflammatory breast neoplasms [SEP] Inflammatory breast neoplasms is metastatic breast cancer characterized by edema and erythema of the affected breast due to lymphatic metastasis and eventual obstruction of lymphatic vessels by the cancer cells.

name: information dissemination
query: Query: information dissemination [SEP] Information dissemination is the circulation or wide dispersal of information.

name: inhalation
query: Query: inhalation [SEP] Inhalation is the act of breathing in.

name: injections , intramuscular
query: Query: injections , intramuscular [SEP] Intramuscular injections is forceful administration into a muscle of liquid medication, nutrient, or other fluid through a hollow needle piercing the muscle and any tissue covering it.

name: injections , intraocular
query: Query: injections , intraocular [SEP] Intraocular injections is the administration of substances into the eye with a hypodermic syringe.

name: ink blot tests
query: Query: ink blot tests [SEP] Ink blot tests is projective tests utilizing ink blots to which a subject responds. They are used in personality diagnosis.

name: insect viruses
query: Query: insect viruses [SEP] Insect viruses is viruses infecting insects, the largest family being baculoviridae.

name: insulin infusion systems
query: Query: insulin infusion systems [SEP] Insulin infusion systems is portable or implantable devices for infusion of insulin. Includes open-loop systems which may be patient-operated or controlled by a pre-set program and are designed for constant delivery of small quantities of insulin, increased during food ingestion, and closed-loop systems which deliver quantities of insulin automatically based on an electronic glucose sensor.

name: intermediate care facilities
query: Query: intermediate care facilities [SEP] Intermediate care facilities is institutions which provide health-related care and services to individuals who do not require the degree of care which hospitals or skilled nursing facilities provide, but because of their physical or mental condition require care and services above the level of room and board.

name: international council of nurses
query: Query: international council of nurses [SEP] International council of nurses is an international professional organization composed of one association per country for the purpose of improving and developing nursing's contribution to the promotion of health and care of the sick.

name: iron isotopes
query: Query: iron isotopes [SEP] Iron isotopes is stable iron atoms that have the same atomic number as the element iron, but differ in atomic weight. Fe-54, 57, and 58 are stable iron isotopes.

name: jaw cysts
query: Query: jaw cysts [SEP] Jaw cysts is saccular lesions lined with epithelium and contained within pathologically formed cavities in the jaw; also nonepithelial cysts (pseudocysts) as they apply to the jaw, e.g., traumatic or solitary cyst, static bone cavity, and aneurysmal bone cyst. True jaw cysts are classified as odontogenic or nonodontogenic.

name: jaw fixation techniques
query: Query: jaw fixation techniques [SEP] Jaw fixation techniques is the stable placement of surgically induced fractures of the mandible or maxilla through the use of elastics, wire ligatures, arch bars, or other splints. It is used often in the cosmetic surgery of retrognathism and prognathism. (From Dorland, 28th ed, p636)

name: jordan
query: Query: jordan [SEP] Jordan is a country in the middle east, northwest of Saudi Arabia, between Israel and Iraq. The capital is Amman.

name: kidney medulla
query: Query: kidney medulla [SEP] Kidney medulla is the internal portion of the kidney, consisting of striated conical masses, the renal pyramids, whose bases are adjacent to the cortex and whose apices form prominent papillae projecting into the lumen of the minor calyces.

name: kidney pelvis
query: Query: kidney pelvis [SEP] Kidney pelvis is the flattened, funnel-shaped expansion connecting the ureter to the kidney calices.

name: knee
query: Query: knee [SEP] Knee is a region of the lower extremity immediately surrounding and including the knee joint.

name: korean war
query: Query: korean war [SEP] Korean war is an armed conflict between Communist and non-Communist forces in Korea from June 25, 1950, to July 27, 1953. The parties included United Nations forces from 15 member nations under United States command against military from North Korea and the Peoples Republic of China.

name: laparotomy
query: Query: laparotomy [SEP] Laparotomy is incision into the side of the abdomen between the ribs and pelvis.

name: legislation , drug
query: Query: legislation , drug [SEP] Drug legislation is laws concerned with manufacturing, dispensing, and marketing of drugs.

name: leishmania major
query: Query: leishmania major [SEP] Leishmania major is a parasitic hemoflagellate of the subgenus Leishmania leishmania that infects man and animals and causes cutaneous leishmaniasis (leishmaniasis, cutaneous) of the Old World. Transmission is by Phlebotomus sandflies.

name: lethal dose 50
query: Query: lethal dose 50 [SEP] Lethal dose 50 is the dose amount of poisonous or toxic substance or dose of ionizing radiation required to kill 50% of the tested population.

name: lewis x antigen
query: Query: lewis x antigen [SEP] Lewis x antigen is a trisaccharide antigen expressed on glycolipids and many cell-surface glycoproteins. In the blood the antigen is found on the surface of neutrophils; eosinophils; and monocytes. In addition, Lewis x antigen is a stage-specific embryonic antigen.

name: life cycle stages
query: Query: life cycle stages [SEP] Life cycle stages is the continuous sequence of changes undergone by living organisms during the post-embryonic developmental process, such as metamorphosis in insects and amphibians. This includes the developmental stages of apicomplexans such as the malarial parasite, plasmodium falciparum.

name: life expectancy
query: Query: life expectancy [SEP] Life expectancy is based on known statistical data, the number of years which any person of a given age may reasonably expected to live.

name: life tables
query: Query: life tables [SEP] Life tables is summarizing techniques used to describe the pattern of mortality and survival in populations. These methods can be applied to the study not only of death, but also of any defined endpoint such as the onset of disease or the occurrence of disease complications.

name: ligase chain reaction
query: Query: ligase chain reaction [SEP] Ligase chain reaction is a dna amplification technique based upon the ligation of oligonucleotide probes. The probes are designed to exactly match two adjacent sequences of a specific target dna. The chain reaction is repeated in three steps in the presence of excess probe: (1) heat denaturation of double-stranded dna, (2) annealing of probes to target dna, and (3) joining of the probes by thermostable dna ligase. After the reaction is repeated for 20-30 cycles the production of ligated probe is measured.

name: lighting
query: Query: lighting [SEP] Lighting is the illumination of an environment and the arrangement of lights to achieve an effect or optimal visibility. Its application is in domestic or in public settings and in medical and non-medical environments.

name: lip
query: Query: lip [SEP] Lip is either of the two fleshy, full-blooded margins of the mouth.

name: lipid droplets
query: Query: lipid droplets [SEP] Lipid droplets is dynamic cytoplasmic organelles found in almost all cells. They consist of a central core of lipids surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer studded with surface proteins, and are involved in lipid metabolism and storage.

name: lip neoplasms

name: posterior tibial tendon dysfunction
query: Query: posterior tibial tendon dysfunction [SEP] Posterior tibial tendon dysfunction is a condition characterized by a broad range of progressive disorders ranging from tenosynovitis to tendon rupture with or without hindfoot collapse to a fixed, rigid, flatfoot deformity. Pathologic changes can involve associated tendons, ligaments, joint structures of the ankle, hindfoot, and midfoot. Posterior tibial tendon dysfunction is the most common cause of acquired flatfoot deformity in adults.

name: postpartum hemorrhage
query: Query: postpartum hemorrhage [SEP] Postpartum hemorrhage is excess blood loss from uterine bleeding associated with obstetric labor or childbirth. It is defined as blood loss greater than 500 ml or of the amount that adversely affects the maternal physiology, such as blood pressure and hematocrit. Postpartum hemorrhage is divided into two categories, immediate (within first 24 hours after birth) or delayed (after 24 hours postpartum).

name: postsynaptic potential summation
query: Query: postsynaptic potential summation [SEP] Postsynaptic potential summation is physiological integration of multiple synaptic potential signals to reach the threshold and initiate postsynaptic action potentials. In spatial summation stimulations from additional synaptic junctions are recruited to generate s response. In temporal summation succeeding stimuli signals are summed up to reach the threshold. The postsynaptic potentials can be either excitatory or inhibitory (epsp or ipsp).

name: potassium iodide
query: Query: potassium iodide [SEP] Potassium iodide is an inorganic compound that is used as a source of iodine in thyrotoxic crisis and in the preparation of thyrotoxic patients for thyroidectomy. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

name: practice management , medical
query: Query: practice management , medical [SEP] Medical practice management is the organization and operation of the business aspects of a physician's practice.

name: practice patterns , nurses '
query: Query: practice patterns , nurses ' [SEP] Nurses' practice patterns is a preferred or standard method of care for nurses.

name: preexisting condition coverage
query: Query: preexisting condition coverage [SEP] Preexisting condition coverage is insurance coverage of a physical or mental health condition, disability, or illness existing before health insurance is applied for or enrolled in.

name: pregnancy tests
query: Query: pregnancy tests [SEP] Pregnancy tests is tests to determine whether or not an individual is pregnant.

name: prenatal care
query: Query: prenatal care [SEP] Prenatal care is care provided the pregnant woman in order to prevent complications, and decrease the incidence of maternal and prenatal mortality.

name: prenatal nutritional physiological phenomena
query: Query: prenatal nutritional physiological phenomena [SEP] Prenatal nutritional physiological phenomena is nutrition of female during pregnancy.

name: preprint
query: Query: preprint [SEP] Preprint is scientific manuscript made available prior to peer review.

name: prescription fees
query: Query: prescription fees [SEP] Prescription fees is the charge levied on the consumer for drugs or therapy prescribed under written order of a physician or other health professional.

name: projection
query: Query: projection [SEP] Projection is a defense mechanism, operating unconsciously, whereby that which is emotionally unacceptable in the self is rejected and attributed (projected) to others.

name: proof of concept study
query: Query: proof of concept study [SEP] Proof of concept study is an empirical investigation which pertains to the development of prototypes or models that demonstrate the feasibility of novel concepts, ideas, principles, schema or their practical application.

name: prostaglandin antagonists
query: Query: prostaglandin antagonists [SEP] Prostaglandin antagonists is compounds that inhibit the action of prostaglandins.

name: protective factors
query: Query: protective factors [SEP] Protective factors is an aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, or inborn or inherited characteristic, which, on the basis of epidemiologic evidence, is known to be associated with prevention or mitigation of a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

name: protein deficiency
query: Query: protein deficiency [SEP] Protein deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of proteins in the diet, characterized by adaptive enzyme changes in the liver, increase in amino acid synthetases, and diminution of urea formation, thus conserving nitrogen and reducing its loss in the urine. Growth, immune response, repair, and production of enzymes and hormones are all impaired in severe protein deficiency. Protein deficiency may also arise in the face of adequate protein intake if the protein is of poor quality (i.e., the content of one or more amino acids is inadequate and thus becomes the limiting factor in protein utilization). (From Merck Manual, 16th ed; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 12th ed, p406)

name: protein denaturation
query: Query: protein denaturation [SEP] Protein denaturation is disruption of the non-covalent bonds and/or disulfide bonds responsible for maintaining the three-dimensional shape and activity of the native protein.

name: psychology , developmental
query: Query: psychology , developmental [SEP] Developmental psychology is field of study concerned with age-related changes in behavior that occur in human beings over the course of life, from birth to death. It includes all aspects of human growth, including emotional, intellectual, social, perceptual and personality development.

name: psychology , military
query: Query: psychology , military [SEP] Military psychology is the branch of applied psychology concerned with psychological aspects of selection, assignment, training, morale, etc., of Armed Forces personnel.

name: psychotherapy , brief
query: Query: psychotherapy , brief [SEP] Brief psychotherapy is any form of psychotherapy designed to produce therapeutic change within a minimal amount of time, generally not more than 20 sessions.

name: psychotherapy , multiple
query: Query: psychotherapy , multiple [SEP] Multiple psychotherapy is the use of more than one therapist at one time in individual or group psychotherapy.

name: public sector
query: Query: public sector [SEP] Public sector is the area of a nation's economy that is tax-supported and under government control.

name: pursuit , smooth
query: Query: pursuit , smooth [SEP] Smooth pursuit is eye movements that are slow, continuous, and conjugate and occur when a fixed object is moved slowly.

name: qi
query: Query: qi [SEP] Qi is the vital life force in the body, supposedly able to be regulated by acupuncture. It corresponds roughly to the Greek pneuma, the Latin spiritus, and the ancient Indian prana. The concept of life-breath or vital energy was formulated as an indication of the awareness of man, originally directed externally toward nature or society but later turned inward to the self or life within. (From Comparison between Concepts of Life-Breath in East and West, 15th International Symposium on the Comparative History of Medicine - East and West, August 26-September 3, 1990, Shizuoka, Japan, pp. ix-x)

name: radiology , interventional
query: Query: radiology , interventional [SEP] Interventional radiology is subspecialty of radiology that combines organ system radiography, catheter techniques and sectional imaging.

name: radon
query: Query: radon [SEP] Radon is a naturally radioactive element with atomic symbol Rn, and atomic number 86. It is a member of the noble gas family found in soil, and is released during the decay of radium.

name: rats , inbred dahl
query: Query: rats , inbred dahl [SEP] Inbred dahl rats is inbred rats derived from Sprague-Dawley rats and used for the study of salt-dependent hypertension. Salt-sensitive and salt-resistant strains have been selectively bred to show the opposite genetically determined blood pressure responses to excess sodium chloride ingestion.

name: receptor , nerve growth factor
query: Query: receptor , nerve growth factor [SEP] Nerve growth factor receptor is a low affinity receptor that binds nerve growth factor; brain-derived neurotrophic factor; neurotrophin 3; and neurotrophin 4.

name: receptors , drug
query: Query: receptors , drug [SEP] Drug receptors is proteins that bind specific drugs with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Drug receptors are generally thought to be receptors for some endogenous substance not otherwise specified.

name: receptors , fibronectin
query: Query: receptors , fibronectin [SEP] Fibronectin receptors is specific cell surface receptors which bind to fibronectins. Studies have shown that these receptors function in certain types of adhesive contact as well as playing a major role in matrix assembly. These receptors include the traditional fibronectin receptor, also called integrin alpha5beta1 and several other integrins.

name: receptors , glucocorticoid
query: Query: receptors , glucocorticoid [SEP] Glucocorticoid receptors is cytoplasmic proteins that specifically bind glucocorticoids and mediate their cellular effects. The glucocorticoid receptor-glucocorticoid complex acts in the nucleus to induce transcription of dna. Glucocorticoids were named for their actions on blood glucose concentration, but they have equally important effects on protein and fat metabolism. Cortisol is the most important example.

name: receptors , glycine
query: Query: receptors , glycine [SEP] Glycine receptors is cell surface receptors that bind glycine with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Glycine receptors in the central nervous system have an intrinsic chloride channel. GlyA receptor is sensitive to strychnine and localized in the post-synaptic membrane of inhibitory glycinergic neurons. GlyB receptor is insensitive to strychnine and associated with the excitatory nmda receptor.

name: receptors , igg
query: Query: receptors , igg [SEP] Igg receptors is specific molecular sites on the surface of various cells, including B-lymphocytes and macrophages, that combine with immunoglobulin Gs. Three subclasses exist: Fc gamma ri (the cd64 antigen, a low affinity receptor), Fc gamma rii (the cd32 antigen, a high affinity receptor), and Fc gamma riii (the cd16 antigen, a low affinity receptor).

name: receptors , notch
query: Query: receptors , notch [SEP] Notch receptors is a family of conserved cell surface receptors that contain epidermal growth factor repeats in their extracellular domain and ankyrin repeats in their cytoplasmic domains. The cytoplasmic domains are released upon ligand binding and translocate to the cell nucleus, where they act as transcription factors.

name: receptors , oxidized ldl
query: Query: receptors , oxidized ldl [SEP] Oxidized ldl receptors is a group of cell-surface receptors for oxidatively modified low-density lipoproteins. The group includes certain scavenger receptors that contribute to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis by uptake of oxidized ldl.

name: recovery room
query: Query: recovery room [SEP] Recovery room is hospital unit providing continuous monitoring of the patient following anesthesia.

name: recurrent laryngeal nerve injuries
query: Query: recurrent laryngeal nerve injuries [SEP] Recurrent laryngeal nerve injuries is traumatic injuries to the recurrent laryngeal nerve that may result in vocal cord dysfunction.

name: recycling
query: Query: recycling [SEP] Recycling is the extraction and recovery of usable or valuable material from scrap or other discarded materials. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed.)

name: reflex , stretch
query: Query: reflex , stretch [SEP] Stretch reflex is reflex contraction of a muscle in response to stretching, which stimulates muscle proprioceptors.

name: reimbursement , incentive
query: Query: reimbursement , incentive [SEP] Incentive reimbursement is a scheme which provides reimbursement for the health services rendered, generally by an institution, and which provides added financial rewards if certain conditions are met. Such a scheme is intended to promote and reward increased efficiency and cost containment, with better care, or at least without adverse effect on the quality of the care rendered.

name: rejection , psychology
query: Query: rejection , psychology [SEP] Psychology rejection is non-acceptance, negative attitudes, hostility or excessive criticism of the individual which may precipitate feelings of rejection.

name: relative energy deficiency in sport
query: Query: relative energy deficiency in sport [SEP] Relative energy deficiency in sport is health disorders associated with low caloric intake of individuals involved in high-activity sports.

name: resource guide
query: Query: resource guide [SEP] Resource guide is work listing and describing various sources of information, from multiple media or in different formats, on a given subject.

name: respiratory distress syndrome , adult
query: Query: respiratory distress syndrome , adult [SEP] Adult respiratory distress syndrome is respiratory distress syndrome , adult

name: retinal artery occlusion
query: Query: retinal artery occlusion [SEP] Retinal artery occlusion is sudden ischemia in the retina due to blocked blood flow through the central retinal artery or its branches leading to sudden complete or partial loss of vision, respectively, in the eye.

name: retraction of publication
query: Query: retraction of publication [SEP] Retraction of publication is work consisting of a statement issued by one or more authors of an article or a book, withdrawing or disavowing acknowledgment of their participation in performing research or writing the results of their study. In indexing, the retraction is sent to the editor of the publication in which the article appeared and is published under the rubric "retraction" or in the form of a letter. This publication type designates the author's statement of retraction: it should be differentiated from retracted publication which labels the retracted publication.

name: retraction of publication as topic
query: Query: retraction of publication as topic [SEP] Retraction of publication as topic is works about authors' withdrawal or disavowal of their participation in performing research or writing the results of their study.

name: rho factor
query: Query: rho factor [SEP] Rho factor is a protein which effects termination of rna synthesis during the genetic transcription process by dissociating the ternary transcription complex rna;-rna polymerase dna at the termination of a gene.

name: rivers
query: Query: rivers [SEP] Rivers is large natural streams of fresh water formed by converging tributaries and which empty into a body of water (lake or ocean).

name: rna , ribosomal
query: Query: rna , ribosomal [SEP] Ribosomal rna is the most abundant form of rna. Together with proteins, it forms the ribosomes, playing a structural role and also a role in ribosomal binding of mRNA and tRNAs. Individual chains are conventionally designated by their sedimentation coefficients. In eukaryotes, four large chains exist, synthesized in the nucleolus and constituting about 50% of the ribosome. (Dorland, 28th ed)

name: rna , transfer , amino acyl
query: Query: rna , transfer , amino acyl [SEP] Amino acyl transfer rna is intermediates in protein biosynthesis. The compounds are formed from amino acids, atp and transfer rna, a reaction catalyzed by aminoacyl tRNA synthetase. They are key compounds in the genetic translation process.

name: rodent control
query: Query: rodent control [SEP] Rodent control is the reduction or regulation of the population of noxious, destructive, or dangerous rodents through chemical, biological, or other means.

name: salmonella food poisoning
query: Query: salmonella food poisoning [SEP] Salmonella food poisoning is poisoning caused by ingestion of food harboring species of salmonella. Conditions of raising, shipping, slaughtering, and marketing of domestic animals contribute to the spread of this bacterium in the food supply.

name: sarcoma , avian
query: Query: sarcoma , avian [SEP] Avian sarcoma is connective tissue tumors, affecting primarily fowl, that are usually caused by avian sarcoma viruses.

name: saudi arabia
query: Query: saudi arabia [SEP] Saudi arabia is a country located in the Middle East, bordering the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea, north of Yemen. The capital is Riyadh.

name: schools , pharmacy
query: Query: schools , pharmacy [SEP] Pharmacy schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of pharmacy.

name: scientific integrity review
query: Query: scientific integrity review [SEP] Scientific integrity review is work consisting of reports by the United States Office of Research Integrity, identifying questionable research published in articles or books. Notification of the questionable data is carried in the nih Guide for Grants and Contracts.

name: seeds
query: Query: seeds [SEP] Seeds is the encapsulated embryos of flowering plants. They are used as is or for animal feed because of the high content of concentrated nutrients like starches, proteins, and fats. Rapeseed, cottonseed, and sunflower seed are also produced for the oils (fats) they yield.

name: selective breeding
query: Query: selective breeding [SEP] Selective breeding is a process in which offspring possessing desired genetic traits are produced.

name: selenium
query: Query: selenium [SEP] Selenium is an element with the atomic symbol Se, atomic number 34, and atomic weight 78.97. It is an essential micronutrient for mammals and other animals but is toxic in large amounts. Selenium protects intracellular structures against oxidative damage. It is an essential component of glutathione peroxidase.

name: self medication
query: Query: self medication [SEP] Self medication is the self administration of medication not prescribed by a physician or in a manner not directed by a physician.

name: sequence homology , nucleic acid
query: Query: sequence homology , nucleic acid [SEP] Nucleic acid sequence homology is the sequential correspondence of nucleotides in one nucleic acid molecule with those of another nucleic acid molecule. Sequence homology is an indication of the genetic relatedness of different organisms and gene function.

name: serum response element
query: Query: serum response element [SEP] Serum response element is a dna sequence that is found in the promoter region of many growth-related genes. The regulatory transcription factor serum response factor binds to and regulates the activity of genes containing this element.

name: sex chromosome aberrations
query: Query: sex chromosome aberrations [SEP] Sex chromosome aberrations is abnormal number or structure of the sex chromosomes. Some sex chromosome aberrations are associated with sex chromosome disorders and sex chromosome disorders of sex development.

name: sick sinus syndrome
query: Query: sick sinus syndrome [SEP] Sick sinus syndrome is a condition caused by dysfunctions related to the sinoatrial node including impulse generation (cardiac sinus arrest) and impulse conduction (sinoatrial exit block). It is characterized by persistent bradycardia, chronic atrial fibrillation, and failure to resume sinus rhythm following cardioversion. This syndrome can be congenital or acquired, particularly after surgical correction for heart defects.

name: singlet oxygen
query: Query: singlet oxygen [SEP] Singlet oxygen is an excited state of molecular oxygen generated photochemically or chemically. Singlet oxygen reacts with a variety of biological molecules such as nucleic acids; proteins; and lipids; causing oxidative damages.

name: single umbilical artery
query: Query: single umbilical artery [SEP] Single umbilical artery is congenital abnormality where one, instead of the usual two, umbilical artery connects the fetus to the placenta.

name: sleep apnea , central
query: Query: sleep apnea , central [SEP] Central sleep apnea is a condition associated with multiple episodes of sleep apnea which are distinguished from obstructive sleep apnea (sleep apnea, obstructive) by the complete cessation of efforts to breathe. This disorder is associated with dysfunction of central nervous system centers that regulate respiration.

name: snail family transcription factors
query: Query: snail family transcription factors [SEP] Snail family transcription factors is a transcription factor family characterized by the presence of several  C-terminal cys2-his2 zinc fingers. They function in many developmental processes including the induction of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition; maintenance of embryonic mesoderm; growth arrest, cell survival; and cell migration.

name: social distance
query: Query: social distance [SEP] Social distance is maintaining recommended amount of spacial separation between self and others.

name: social perception
query: Query: social perception [SEP] Social perception is the perceiving of attributes, characteristics, and behaviors of one's associates or social groups.

name: social stigma
query: Query: social stigma [SEP] Social stigma is a perceived attribute that is deeply discrediting and is considered to be a violation of social norms.

name: software validation
query: Query: software validation [SEP] Software validation is the act of testing the software for compliance with a standard.

name: soil microbiology
query: Query: soil microbiology [SEP] Soil microbiology is the presence of bacteria, viruses, and fungi in the soil. This term is not restricted to pathogenic organisms.

name: solar energy
query: Query: solar energy [SEP] Solar energy is energy transmitted from the sun in the form of electromagnetic radiation.

name: solitary kidney
query: Query: solitary kidney [SEP] Solitary kidney is either a single or a single functioning kidney due to nephrectomy, birth defects or other kidney diseases.

name: sound localization
query: Query: sound localization [SEP] Sound localization is ability to determine the specific location of a sound source.

name: soybean proteins
query: Query: soybean proteins [SEP] Soybean proteins is proteins which are present in or isolated from soybeans.

name: sperm transport
query: Query: sperm transport [SEP] Sperm transport is passive or active movement of spermatozoa from the testicular seminiferous tubules through the male reproductive tract as well as within the female reproductive tract.

name: standardized nursing terminology
query: Query: standardized nursing terminology [SEP] Standardized nursing terminology is standardized terms used in the nursing field (e.g., nursing informatics).

name: state government
query: Query: state government [SEP] State government is the level of governmental organization and function below that of the national or country-wide government.

name: stenosis , pulmonary vein
query: Query: stenosis , pulmonary vein [SEP] Pulmonary vein stenosis is narrowing of the pulmonary vein.

name: suction
query: Query: suction [SEP] Suction is the removal of secretions, gas or fluid from hollow or tubular organs or cavities by means of a tube and a device that acts on negative pressure.

name: superficial back muscles
query: Query: superficial back muscles [SEP] Superficial back muscles is the top layer of the back muscles whose function is to move the scapula. This group of muscles consists of the trapezius, latissimus dorsi, rhomboid major, rhomboid minor and levator scapulae.

name: superior mesenteric artery syndrome
query: Query: superior mesenteric artery syndrome [SEP] Superior mesenteric artery syndrome is duodenal obstruction by the superior mesenteric artery (mesenteric artery, superior) which travels in the root of the mesentery and crosses over the duodenum. The syndrome is characterized by the dilated proximal duodenum and stomach, bloating, abdominal cramps, and vomiting. Often it is observed in patient with body casts after spinal surgery.

name: surgical wound
query: Query: surgical wound [SEP] Surgical wound is an incision made during a surgical procedure.

name: survivin
query: Query: survivin [SEP] Survivin is an apoptosis inhibitory protein that contains a single baculoviral iap repeat (bir) domain. It associates with microtubules and functions to regulate cell proliferation as a component of the chromosome passage protein complex (cpc), performing essential roles for localization of the complex, chromosome alignment, segregation during mitosis and cytokinesis, and assembly of the mitotic spindle. It is expressed by fetal kidney and liver cells and highly expressed in adenocarcinoma and high-grade lymphoma.

name: suture techniques
query: Query: suture techniques [SEP] Suture techniques is techniques for securing together the edges of a wound, with loops of thread or similar materials (sutures).

name: swimming
query: Query: swimming [SEP] Swimming is an activity in which the body is propelled through water by specific movement of the arms and/or the legs. Swimming as propulsion through water by the movement of limbs, tail, or fins of animals is often studied as a form of physical exertion or endurance.

name: syphilis , cutaneous
query: Query: syphilis , cutaneous [SEP] Cutaneous syphilis is cutaneous lesions arising from infection with Treponema pallidum. In the primary stage, 18-21 days following infection, one or more chancres appear. If untreated, the subsequent stages of the disease appear as syphilids. These eruptions are superficial, nondestructive, exanthematic, transient, macular roseolas that may later be maculopapular or papular polymorphous or scaly, pustular, pigmented eruptions.(Arnold, Odom, and James, Andrew's Diseases of the Skin, 8th ed, p409)

name: teacher training
query: Query: teacher training [SEP] Teacher training is a curriculum-centered process of equipping individuals with professional knowledge and skills required to become effective teachers.

name: thyroid hormone receptors alpha
query: Query: thyroid hormone receptors alpha [SEP] Thyroid hormone receptors alpha is high affinity receptors for thyroid hormones, especially triiodothyronine. These receptors are usually found in the nucleus where they regulate dna transcription. They are encoded by the thra gene (also known as nr1a1, thra1, erba or erba1 gene) as several isoforms produced by alternative splicing.

name: tibial arteries
query: Query: tibial arteries [SEP] Tibial arteries is the anterior and posterior arteries created at the bifurcation of the popliteal artery. The anterior tibial artery begins at the lower border of the popliteus muscle and lies along the tibia at the distal part of the leg to surface superficially anterior to the ankle joint. Its branches are distributed throughout the leg, ankle, and foot. The posterior tibial artery begins at the lower border of the popliteus muscle, lies behind the tibia in the lower part of its course, and is found situated between the medial malleolus and the medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity. Its branches are distributed throughout the leg and foot.

name: tobacco use cessation devices
query: Query: tobacco use cessation devices [SEP] Tobacco use cessation devices is devices or delivery systems used to aid in ending a tobacco habit.

name: tooth bleaching agents
query: Query: tooth bleaching agents [SEP] Tooth bleaching agents is chemicals that are used to oxidize pigments in teeth and thus effect whitening.

name: tooth crown
query: Query: tooth crown [SEP] Tooth crown is the upper part of the tooth, which joins the lower part of the tooth (tooth root) at the cervix (tooth cervix) at a line called the cementoenamel junction. The entire surface of the crown is covered with enamel which is thicker at the extremity and becomes progressively thinner toward the cervix. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p216)

name: toxicity tests , chronic
query: Query: toxicity tests , chronic [SEP] Chronic toxicity tests is experiments designed to determine the potential toxic effects of a long-term exposure to a chemical or chemicals.

name: tracheal neoplasms
query: Query: tracheal neoplasms [SEP] Tracheal neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the trachea.

name: travel nursing
query: Query: travel nursing [SEP] Travel nursing is a type of nursing practice involving licensed professional nurses who travel to work in temporary nursing positions.

name: tropical climate
query: Query: tropical climate [SEP] Tropical climate is a climate which is typical of equatorial and tropical regions, i.e., one with continually high temperatures with considerable precipitation, at least during part of the year. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: troponin i
query: Query: troponin i [SEP] Troponin i is a troponin complex subunit that inhibits actomyosin atpase activity thereby disrupting actin and myosin interaction. There are three troponin i subtypes: troponin i1, i2 and i3. Troponin i3 is cardiac-specific whereas troponin i1 and i2 are skeletal subtypes. Troponin i3 is a biomarker for damaged or injured cardiac myocytes and mutations in troponin i3 gene are associated with familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

name: tuberculosis , central nervous system
query: Query: tuberculosis , central nervous system [SEP] Central nervous system tuberculosis is tuberculosis of the brain, spinal cord, or meninges (tuberculosis, meningeal), most often caused by mycobacterium tuberculosis and rarely by mycobacterium bovis. The infection may be limited to the nervous system or coexist in other organs (e.g., tuberculosis, pulmonary). The organism tends to seed the meninges causing a diffuse meningitis and leads to the formation of tuberculoma, which may occur within the brain, spinal cord, or perimeningeal spaces. Tuberculous involvement of the vertebral column (tuberculosis, spinal) may result in nerve root or spinal cord compression. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp717-20)

name: tumor hypoxia
query: Query: tumor hypoxia [SEP] Tumor hypoxia is hypoxic conditions in tumor cells due to the tumor outgrowing its blood supply. It is associated with increased metastasis and resistance to radiotherapy and drug therapy.

name: turner syndrome
query: Query: turner syndrome [SEP] Turner syndrome is a syndrome of defective gonadal development in phenotypic females associated with the karyotype 45,x (or 45,xo). Patients generally are of short stature with undifferentiated gonads (streak gonads), sexual infantilism, hypogonadism, webbing of the neck, cubitus valgus, elevated gonadotropins, decreased estradiol level in blood, and congenital heart defects. noonan syndrome (also called Pseudo-Turner Syndrome and Male Turner Syndrome) resembles this disorder; however, it occurs in males and females with a normal karyotype and is inherited as an autosomal dominant.

name: type b personality
query: Query: type b personality [SEP] Type b personality is behavior pattern characterized by a generally calm and even-tempered demeanor. Emotionally, such personality types show less frequent irritation, anger, hostility, and aggression than Type a individuals. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 223)

name: ulcer
query: Query: ulcer [SEP] Ulcer is a lesion on the surface of the skin or a mucous surface, produced by the sloughing of inflammatory necrotic tissue.

name: unconscious , psychology
query: Query: unconscious , psychology [SEP] Psychology unconscious is those forces and content of the mind which are not ordinarily available to conscious awareness or to immediate recall.

name: unemployment
query: Query: unemployment [SEP] Unemployment is the state of not being engaged in a gainful occupation.

name: unified medical language system
query: Query: unified medical language system [SEP] Unified medical language system is a research and development program initiated by the national library of medicine to build knowledge sources for the purpose of aiding the development of systems that help health professionals retrieve and integrate biomedical information. The knowledge sources can be used to link disparate information systems to overcome retrieval problems caused by differences in terminology and the scattering of relevant information across many databases. The three knowledge sources are the Metathesaurus, the Semantic Network, and the Specialist Lexicon.

name: united states occupational safety and health administration
query: Query: united states occupational safety and health administration [SEP] United states occupational safety and health administration is an office in the Department of Labor responsible for developing and establishing occupational safety and health standards.

name: universal health insurance
query: Query: universal health insurance [SEP] Universal health insurance is health insurance coverage for all persons in a state or country, rather than for some subset of the population. It may extend to the unemployed as well as to the employed; to aliens as well as to citizens; for pre-existing conditions as well as for current illnesses; for mental as well as for physical conditions.

name: upper extremity deep vein thrombosis
query: Query: upper extremity deep vein thrombosis [SEP] Upper extremity deep vein thrombosis is deep vein thrombosis of an upper extremity vein (e.g., axillary vein; subclavian vein; and jugular veins). It is associated with mechanical factors (Upper Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis, Primary) secondary to other anatomic factors (Upper Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis, Secondary). Symptoms may include sudden onset of pain, warmth, redness, blueness, and swelling in the arm.

name: urbanization
query: Query: urbanization [SEP] Urbanization is the process whereby a society changes from a rural to an urban way of life. It refers also to the gradual increase in the proportion of people living in urban areas.

name: urinary bladder
query: Query: urinary bladder [SEP] Urinary bladder is a musculomembranous sac along the urinary tract. urine flows from the kidneys into the bladder via the ureters (ureter), and is held there until urination.

name: urology department , hospital
query: Query: urology department , hospital [SEP] Hospital urology department is hospital department responsible for the administration and provision of diagnostic and therapeutic services for the urologic patient.

name: vaccines , marker
query: Query: vaccines , marker [SEP] Marker vaccines is vaccines used in conjunction with diagnostic tests to differentiate vaccinated animals from carrier animals. Marker vaccines can be either a subunit or a gene-deleted vaccine.

name: vaginal absorption
query: Query: vaginal absorption [SEP] Vaginal absorption is the uptake of substances from the vagina via the vaginal epithelium/mucosa.

name: vaginal discharge
query: Query: vaginal discharge [SEP] Vaginal discharge is a common gynecologic disorder characterized by an abnormal, nonbloody discharge from the genital tract.

name: vaginal fistula
query: Query: vaginal fistula [SEP] Vaginal fistula is an abnormal anatomical passage that connects the vagina to other organs, such as the bladder (vesicovaginal fistula) or the rectum (rectovaginal fistula).

name: vancomycin resistance
query: Query: vancomycin resistance [SEP] Vancomycin resistance is nonsusceptibility of bacteria to the action of vancomycin, an inhibitor of cell wall synthesis.

name: vascular closure devices
query: Query: vascular closure devices [SEP] Vascular closure devices is products used to seal the openings in blood vessels from incisions or punctures made during endovascular procedures.

name: vascular neoplasms
query: Query: vascular neoplasms [SEP] Vascular neoplasms is neoplasms located in the vasculature system, such as arteries and veins. They are differentiated from neoplasms of vascular tissue (neoplasms, vascular tissue), such as angiofibroma or hemangioma.

name: ventral thalamic nuclei
query: Query: ventral thalamic nuclei [SEP] Ventral thalamic nuclei is a large group of nuclei lying between the internal medullary lamina and the internal capsule. It includes the ventral anterior, ventral lateral, and ventral posterior nuclei.

name: veterans health services
query: Query: veterans health services [SEP] Veterans health services is services organized for the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and maintenance of health primarily of veterans.

name: viral tail proteins
query: Query: viral tail proteins [SEP] Viral tail proteins is proteins found in the tail sections of dna and rna viruses. It is believed that these proteins play a role in directing chain folding and assembly of polypeptide chains.

name: virology
query: Query: virology [SEP] Virology is the study of the structure, growth, function, genetics, and reproduction of viruses, and virus diseases.

name: viscosity
query: Query: viscosity [SEP] Viscosity is the resistance that a gaseous or liquid system offers to flow when it is subjected to shear stress. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: vision disparity
query: Query: vision disparity [SEP] Vision disparity is the difference between two images on the retina when looking at a visual stimulus. This occurs since the two retinas do not have the same view of the stimulus because of the location of our eyes. Thus the left eye does not get exactly the same view as the right eye.

name: vitamin k 3

name: vitreous body
query: Query: vitreous body [SEP] Vitreous body is the transparent, semigelatinous substance that fills the cavity behind the crystalline lens of the eye and in front of the retina. It is contained in a thin hyaloid membrane and forms about four fifths of the optic globe.

name: warm ischemia
query: Query: warm ischemia [SEP] Warm ischemia is a tissue or organ remaining at physiological temperature during decreased blood perfusion or in the absence of blood supply. During organ transplantation it begins when the organ reaches physiological temperature before the completion of surgical anastomosis and ends with reestablishment of the blood circulation through the tissue.

query: Query: washington [SEP] Washington is state bounded by on the north by Canada, on the east by Idaho, on the south by Oregon, and on the west by the Pacific Ocean.

name: water purification
query: Query: water purification [SEP] Water purification is any of several processes in which undesirable impurities in water are removed or neutralized; for example, chlorination, filtration, primary treatment, ion exchange, and distillation. It includes treatment of waste water to provide potable and hygienic water in a controlled or closed environment as well as provision of public drinking water supplies.

name: wavelet analysis
query: Query: wavelet analysis [SEP] Wavelet analysis is signal and data processing method that uses decomposition of wavelets to approximate, estimate, or compress signals with finite time and frequency domains. It represents a signal or data in terms of a fast decaying wavelet series from the original prototype wavelet, called the mother wavelet. This mathematical algorithm has been adopted widely in biomedical disciplines for data and signal processing in noise removal and audio/image compression (e.g., eeg and mri).

name: white muscle disease
query: Query: white muscle disease [SEP] White muscle disease is a myodegeneration most frequent in calves and lambs whose dams have been fed during gestation or longer on feeds, especially legumes (fabaceae), grown in certain areas where selenium is either deficient or unavailable in the soil. It has been recorded in many countries. It has been produced experimentally in several species of animals on low-selenium intake. a similar myopathy occurs naturally in goats, deer, foals, and dogs but proof of the etiology is lacking. (Merck Veterinary Manual, 5th ed)

name: working poor

name: yang deficiency
query: Query: yang deficiency [SEP] Yang deficiency is in the yin-yang system of philosophy and medicine, a lack of vital energy (called yangxu in Chinese). It manifests itself in various systemic and organic diseases. (The Pinyin Chinese-English Dictionary, 1979)
